title: Return from a thread to the same view, selection and scroll position
body:
**Usability proposal. Priority: P2; first navigation improvement.** Reviewed 2026-09-06 at `6c7a6fbe`.

### User outcome
Open a thread from a board or report, inspect it, then return to exactly where you were. Reviewing a list should not require rebuilding it after every item.

### Evidence
App.handleSelectThread sets view to thread. App renders the center views conditionally, unmounting the source view. Planboard owns projectId and sort locally; Usage owns range, metric and breakdown locally. There is no source-view return context in these callbacks. A mounted Planboard changed to number-asc returns to updated after unmount/remount with identical props. This is a component reproduction plus an App wiring trace, not a desktop navigation recording.

### Smallest useful scope
- Capture one return destination when opening a thread from Planboard live plans, Kanban, Activity, Digest, PRs or Insights.
- Offer a clear keyboard-accessible “Back to [view]” action in the thread header.
- Restore the source view's project, existing filters/sort/range/group, list position and originating row focus.
- Reuse a small App-owned view-state record. Do not keep every hidden report mounted and polling, add a router, or create multi-level navigation history.
- Session-only restoration is enough. Do not add persistence across app restarts.

### Acceptance
- Set Planboard sort, open a live-plan thread and return: same project and sort remain.
- Open a row halfway down Activity/Digest/PRs/Insights; return to that row, with a sensible nearest-row fallback if it disappeared.
- Switching reports preserves the user's existing Usage controls.
- A missing/deleted project or thread gives a safe fallback rather than restoring an invalid selection.
- Return navigation cannot submit a prompt, launch a run, or restore a pending destructive action.
- Validate with an App-level navigation test and browser checks for scroll/focus.

Distinct from composer-draft preservation #921, named sidebar filters #939 and review itinerary #421. Preserve the daily-work/Pulse split introduced in #425.

Sources: [selection callback](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/App.tsx#L391), [conditional views](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/App.tsx#L1357), [Planboard local state](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/PlanboardView.tsx#L82).
Runnable evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --import=./test/support/render.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-views-evidence.mjs` (exit 0). This audit script asserts current behavior, not desired regression behavior. Artifact is in the audit checkout; reproduction steps above are self-contained.

Requested disposition: separate Planboard issue with plan:todo. No implementation in this research task.

title: Activity and Digest must distinguish load failures from empty results
body:
**Reproduced usability bug. Priority: P1.** Reviewed 2026-09-06 at `6c7a6fbe`.

### Problem and reproduction
1. Load Activity successfully with one event. Reject the next listActivity call and press Refresh.
2. Existing rows disappear and the view says “No activity yet”, with no failure explanation.
3. Separately mount Digest with loadDigest rejecting.
4. It says “Nothing ran while you were away.” and Mark reviewed remains enabled.

These are statements about work that happened, but the app has failed to retrieve that work. In Digest the user can also invoke acknowledgement without seeing a successfully loaded digest.

### Cause
ActivityView.loadAll catches errors with setItems([]). DigestView.loadAll catches with setResult(null). Both feed the ordinary empty rendering branch. onMarkReviewed also silently returns if markSeen rejects.

### Smallest useful scope
- Initial failure: explicit load error and Retry.
- Refresh failure: retain the last successful rows, label them as potentially out of date, expose Retry.
- Show successful-empty copy only after a successful response.
- Disable Mark reviewed while there is no successfully loaded digest or acknowledgement is pending; clearly surface acknowledgement failure.
- Do not silently clear a digest window after a failed acknowledgement.
- Reuse the existing InsightsView approach, which already retains modes and displays refresh errors. No shared fetching framework is needed.

### Acceptance
Tests cover initial rejection, refresh rejection after success, successful empty response, retry recovery and markSeen rejection. A failed refresh does not erase known data or claim that no work occurred. Errors are announced accessibly and buttons remain reachable.

This concerns local Activity/Digest rendering and acknowledgement, not forge outage resilience #427 or decorative chrome #729/#728.

Sources: [Activity load](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/ActivityView.tsx#L28), [Digest load and acknowledgement](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/DigestView.tsx#L64), [existing Insights pattern](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/InsightsView.tsx#L20).
Runnable evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --import=./test/support/render.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-views-evidence.mjs` (exit 0). This audit script asserts current behavior, not desired regression behavior. Artifact is in the audit checkout; reproduction steps above are self-contained.

Requested disposition: separate Planboard issue with plan:todo. No implementation in this research task.

title: Show and change project scope inside Activity and Kanban
body:
**Usability proposal. Priority: P2. Small scope.** Reviewed 2026-09-06 at `6c7a6fbe`.

### User outcome
Know whether a board/feed shows one project or the whole workspace, and change that scope without leaving the view or reopening a sidebar drawer.

### Evidence and reproduction
#598 correctly passes a sidebar scope when opening Activity/Kanban. Both components filter their data by projectScope. Their headers show only the view title (plus Refresh in Activity). Mount either with a selected project and no matching rows: the empty state does not identify which project is empty. Neither component has an in-view scope selector. On a narrow layout the sidebar scope can be out of sight.

### Smallest useful scope
- Put a compact labelled Project selector in each header, including “All projects”.
- Seed it from the existing sidebar-open behavior; keep #598 intact.
- Route changes through App's existing activityProjectId/kanbanProjectId state.
- Show scope explicitly in empty results with a clear Show all projects escape.
- Preserve the view's scope when returning from a thread. Do not make an unrelated sidebar filter change silently change an already-open report.
- Do not introduce a new global filter system or force workspace-wide Pulse reports into project scope.

### Acceptance
Open with a sidebar project scope: header names that project and rows match it. Switch to All projects: rows across projects return. A scoped empty result names the project and offers a way out. With sidebar closed at narrow widths, scope remains visible and keyboard operable. Handle removal of the selected project explicitly.

This builds on completed #597/#598. It is distinct from #939 named sidebar filter sets and #728/#729 CSS work.

Sources: [Activity scope and header](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/ActivityView.tsx#L56), [Kanban scope and header](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/KanbanView.tsx#L66), [App scope callbacks](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/App.tsx#L405).
Runnable evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --import=./test/support/render.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-views-evidence.mjs` (exit 0). title: Find Planboard cards by title or issue number without scanning every column
body:
**Usability proposal. Priority: P2. Small scope.** Reviewed 2026-09-06 at `6c7a6fbe`.

### User outcome
Find a known issue in a large backlog, then start or open it directly.

### Evidence
Planboard renders every supplied issue into its status columns. The header has project, launch mode/profile, sorting and Refresh controls but no search. Card labels are display-only. A user who knows an issue title or number must scan columns or leave for GitHub. #655 concerns fetching the complete backlog, not finding a card within it.

### Smallest useful scope
- Add a labelled native search input: “Find issues by title or number”.
- Case-insensitive title matching and exact numeric matching for both 123 and #123.
- Filter locally over the complete issue result already loaded. Do not add an index, fuzzy-search dependency or new network endpoint.
- Keep current columns and sorting. Display visible/total counts while searching.
- “No matching issues” and Clear search must be distinct from a genuinely empty plan.
- Clearly scope the search to issue cards. Keep live agent plans separate and labelled.
- Keep project, search and Refresh readily accessible. Put secondary launch options on a wrapping secondary row when needed rather than expanding the fixed-height header indefinitely.

### Acceptance
A large fixture can find issues by case-insensitive title or #number across statuses; clearing restores all rows and original ordering. No result does not show “Nothing on the plan yet”. Existing Start task behavior works for filtered cards. Keyboard focus and controls stay usable in narrow main panes and at increased UI scale.

Do not rebuild #655 pagination, #251 dependencies, or add saved searches already covered for the sidebar in #939. This is behavior, outside the CSS-only #728 scope.

Source: [Planboard controls and columns](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/PlanboardView.tsx#L210). Audit mount confirms no search input; source review confirms there is no issue-query state.
Runnable evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --import=./test/support/render.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-views-evidence.mjs` (exit 0). This audit script asserts current behavior, not desired regression behavior. Artifact is in the audit checkout; reproduction steps above are self-contained.

title: Open the source thread directly from the Usage breakdown
body:
**Usability proposal. Priority: P2. Small scope.** Reviewed 2026-09-06 at `6c7a6fbe`.

### User outcome
Answer “why did this thread use so much?” directly from Usage, without copying its title into the sidebar and searching again.

### Evidence
Usage already offers Model / Day / Project / Thread breakdowns from #556. The thread rows render their labels as plain table cells. UsageViewProps contains no onSelectThread callback and App supplies none. The numbers identify a thread but the view has no way to open it. This is a source-confirmed interaction gap, not a missing cost calculation.

### Smallest useful scope
- Render the thread title in Thread breakdown as an accessible link/button that opens the existing thread.
- Use its stable thread ID, not a title lookup; duplicate titles must open the right thread.
- Integrate with the source-view return behavior so range, Cost/Tokens and Thread breakdown survive inspection.
- Keep rows whose transcript was deleted visible for honest historical accounting, but show an unavailable explanation rather than a broken action.
- No new analytics, aggregate recomputation, charts, export pipeline or separate detail page.

### Acceptance
Click or keyboard activation opens exactly the thread represented by the row. Deleted/missing threads do not crash or navigate to another thread. Numeric cells remain selectable and do not become an oversized click target. Returning preserves the report controls. Unreported/unmetered cost labels and existing #556 caveats remain.

This extends the shipped breakdown in #152/#556; it does not recreate either. Follow the existing onSelectThread interaction used by Digest/Insights.

Sources: [Usage props](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/UsageView.tsx#L21), [breakdown cells](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/UsageView.tsx#L400), [App view wiring](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/App.tsx#L1357).

Requested disposition: separate Planboard issue with plan:todo. No implementation in this research task.
